title: Studio work and cliques for Black musicians
summary: He says studio contracting is still political and few Black musicians get work outside jazz.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What about the whole studio thing? You remember we talked on the other tape about the whole idea

of the Black musician getting into the studios at that time when it was supposed to be a half and half band, but you were the only one finally that got the job? Then what happened after that, once you got into the studios? How did it evolve?
Well, it hasn't evolved yet. Still difficult. You have to go through contractors.
And it seems to be a clique.

Cliques, you know. It's a political ballgame. And then you get the seniority bit. If you've never been there, you never get any seniority. But out of the thousands of musicians that there are, there are very few Black musicians that are working in any phase of it, except jazz, and that's looked down upon government-wise, as far as funding goes. They give millions to the symphony orchestras.

Beethoven (Inaudible) hasn't changed since he's given what he did, but Luther Anderson changed his support. Fred Norman was a guy -- Fred Norman's been around as long as I can remember trying to get a job as an arranger, and he's one of the finest arrangers there is.

You have to be brash or flaky, you know, to gain attention. You can't just be Al Hall, you know. You got to be something else to get attention. You can't take anything for granted. You got to be in there pitching all the time, to make sure that you get your piece of the action.
And once you let down, there's somebody else right over you.
And then, of course, there might be someone undermining you while you're learning --

There's always someone undermining you, My goal in life was never to be at the very, very top. I just wanted to be good at whatever I had to do. And consequently the different styles of music I've been playing. But once you're on top, you're going to get toppled. There's no place else to go, and -- but I just want to be able to do whatever I'm called upon to do. And luckily enough, I've had a lot of people who have hired me just on that basis.
